statement.p: Use the Chain Rule to evaluate the partial derivative \frac{\partial g}{\partial \theta} at the point (r,\theta)=(2\sqrt 2,\frac{\pi}4)
where g(x,y) = \frac{1}{2 x+8 y^2}, x=r\sin\theta, y=r\cos\theta.

static.solution:
g( x,y )=\frac{1}{2 x+8 {y}^2}: \frac{\partial g}{\partial x}=-\frac{2}{{(2 x+8 {y}^2)}^2},\quad \frac{\partial g}{\partial y}=-\frac{16 y}{{(2 x+8 {y}^2)}^2} By the Chain Rule we have \begin{array}{rcl} \frac{\partial g}{\partial \theta }\amp =\amp \frac{\partial g}{\partial x} \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta }+\frac{\partial g}{\partial y} \frac{\partial y}{\partial \theta }\\ \amp =\amp -\frac{2}{{(2 x+8 {y}^2)}^2} \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta }-\frac{16 y}{{(2 x+8 {y}^2)}^2} \frac{\partial y}{\partial \theta }\\ \amp =\amp -\frac{1}{{(2 x+8 {y}^2)}^2}\left(2\frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta }+16 y \frac{\partial y}{\partial \theta }\right) \end{array} We find the partial derivatives \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta }, \frac{\partial y}{\partial \theta }: \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta }=r \cos \theta ,\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial \theta }=-r \sin \theta Hence, \frac{\partial g}{\partial \theta }=-\frac{r}{{(2 x+8 {y}^2)}^2} (2\cos\theta -16 y \sin \theta ) \quad \mathbf{(1)} At the point ( r,\theta )=\bigl(2\sqrt{2},\frac{\pi }{4}\bigr), we have x=2\sqrt{2} \sin \frac{\pi }{4}=2 and y=2\sqrt{2} \cos \frac{\pi }{4}=2.
Substituting ( r,\theta )=\bigl(2\sqrt{2},\frac{\pi }{4}\bigr) and ( x,y )=( 2,2 ) in \mathbf{(1)} gives the following derivative: \begin{array}{rcl} \left.\frac{\partial g}{\partial \theta }\right|_{( r,\theta)=\left(2\sqrt{2},\frac{\pi}{4}\right)} \amp =\amp \frac{-2\sqrt{2}}{{(4+8\cdot {2}^2)}^2} \left(2\cos \frac{\pi }{4}-32 \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\\ \amp =\amp \frac{-\sqrt{2}}{648}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{32}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=\frac{15}{324}. \end{array}
